name: Sensing architecture and data governance
consequences: Tiered sensing architecture reduces privacy risk and data handling burden on routine nights, enabling safer broader sharing and easier integration into a data warehouse. It also introduces escalation points that require coordination and may delay capturing infrequent events if responders are unavailable, creating potential data gaps during peak periods. Edge-case policy adjustments and staff training may be required.
options: Implement a tiered sensing protocol prioritizing dry-electrode EEG and mattress sensors for baseline nights, enabling full PSG only on escalation nights after predefined triggers.
Institute strict de-identification and access controls across datasets before external collaboration, anchored by a data steward and formal audit trails.
Establish formal data use agreements and partner registries to ensure traceable, compliant data sharing while maintaining core privacy protections.
review: Tiered sensing offers privacy protection and data richness, but escalation triggers risk gaps if responders cannot reach events in time, potentially delaying Aim 1 milestones.

name: Staffing model and shift design for 8 active suites
consequences: Ensures safety coverage across all 8 active suites and supports timely event response and annotation throughput. However, external standby staff increases variable costs and demands additional onboarding and training alignment with core team workflows.
options: Institute rotating night shifts with cross-trained technicians to ensure safety response and consistent annotation throughput across all active suites.
Adopt structured overlapping shifts with an on-call escalation mechanism to balance safety requirements with predictable labor costs.
Contract external standby staff for peak-risk periods, preserving core team stability while managing variability in event response.
review: Flexible staffing enhances safety coverage across eight suites, yet reliance on external supplemental staff can erode consistency and raise cost volatility if onboarding lags.

name: Event-triage tool development and validation
consequences: Advancing triage capabilities will reduce manual review workload and accelerate phenotyping, but early accuracy depends on data quality and inter-rater consistency, which can delay milestones. Effective validation is essential to maintain confidence in phenotyping results.
options: Develop a data-driven event-triage model trained on adjudicated episodes, incorporating a robust human-in-the-loop validation workflow.
Adopt a transparent rule-based triage framework with pre-defined criteria to prioritize clinician review and preserve interpretability.
Limit automated triage to retrospective analysis during the initial phase, ensuring patient safety through manual scoring during real-time monitoring.
review: Developing a triage model reduces manual scoring, but early accuracy hinges on data quality and scorer consistency, risking slower progress toward the Aim 2 phenotyping milestone.

name: Recruitment pathways and retention safeguards
consequences: Improved recruitment trajectory accelerates enrollment toward target; however, too lenient criteria may increase heterogeneity and affect interpretability of longitudinal patterns. Maintaining strict pre-admission screening can safeguard safety but may slow initial enrollment.
options: Coordinate recruitment through University Hospital Bonn, regional neurologists, and professional networks, implementing structured pre-admission screening and collateral history to reduce dropouts.
Provide enhanced participant engagement through clear milestones, regular feedback, and transparent expectations to improve retention during extended stays.
Implement adaptive inclusion criteria reviews at predefined milestones to maintain enrollment targets without compromising safety.
review: Recruitment optimization accelerates enrollment, but overly broad criteria may increase heterogeneity and complicate interpretation of longitudinal patterns.

name: Environmental design and safety balance
consequences: Preserves naturalistic behavior supports data fidelity and participant comfort, yet safety features may introduce perceptible cues that change sleep behavior, requiring careful monitoring and gradual adjustments during the pilot phase.
options: Maintain a home-like interior with discreet safety upgrades and rapid access points to ensure safety without compromising naturalistic behavior.
Introduce visible safety control points and secure observation spaces that reassure staff while preserving a domestic ambience.
Develop flexible room configurations that can adapt to increased event density while maintaining participant comfort.
review: Environmental design preserves comfort and data fidelity, yet safety features may introduce perceptible cues that change sleep behavior, requiring careful monitoring and gradual adjustments during the pilot phase.

name: Budget governance and milestone gating
consequences: Linking spending to progress drives accountability but rigid gates may delay critical hires or equipment procurement if milestones slip, risking data quality or recruitment pace.
options: Institute milestone-based expenditures with quarterly reviews that reallocate funds toward data quality improvements and recruitment acceleration.
Prioritize core operations in year one with a contingency reserve for equipment upgrades and regulatory approvals to prevent disruption.
Engage external audits and scenario planning to detect potential overruns early and preserve sustainability across all three years.
review: Budget governance aligns spending with progress, but rigid gates may delay critical hires or equipment procurement if milestones slip, risking data quality or recruitment pace.

name: Phased intake cadence aligned to data quality milestones
consequences: Staged participant intake aligns with safety reviews and data pipeline validation, reducing bottlenecks in annotation throughput during the pilot phase. Downstream, full capacity deployment is contingent on achieving data quality milestones, which may delay rapid scaling to 12 suites and extend the time to reach enrollment targets.
options: Implement a phased intake cadence that ramps stays from 8 active suites to full capacity only after initial data-quality milestones are met.
Adopt rolling enrollment with fixed weekly intake windows to maintain consistent staffing and annotation throughput regardless of individual event yield.
Prioritize high-risk participants into early cohorts with enhanced monitoring to validate safety protocols before expanding to the broader pool.
review: Rolling intake aligned to data milestones stabilizes early data collection, but may slow scaling if milestones slip and occupancy lags behind planned expansion.

name: Cross-domain data access governance with privacy-preserving pipelines
consequences: This approach creates formal data-use boundaries and audit trails, enabling de-identified sharing with collaborators while maintaining privacy controls. The trade-off is increased governance overhead and potential delays in data availability for external validation until approvals are updated.
options: Implement de-identified data export with controlled tokens and revocation, enabling selective external collaboration without compromising patient privacy.
Establish a formal data-use agreement template and review cadence to synchronize access rights with evolving project milestones.
Institute a privacy-preserving federated analysis pilot that avoids raw data transfers while enabling multi-site validation.
review: Cross-domain governance enables compliant collaboration, but adds review cycles that can delay data sharing and slow external validation until agreements and templates are fully established.

name: Facility modularity and safety-enabled room reconfiguration
consequences: Rooms can be reconfigured for enhanced safety or expanded capacity; downstream, expansion to 12 suites can be achieved with minimal renovation disruption, but requires upfront modular equipment and logistics coordination. This approach reduces long-run renovation risk but introduces upfront procurement complexity.
options: Install modular partition systems and adjustable safety features to reconfigure spaces quickly for different study phases.
Adopt a phased renovation blueprint that pre-install scalable infrastructure and flexible utilities to support future expansion.
Create a safety-first room design library mapping risk profiles to configurable layout templates and staffing plans.
review: Modularity supports rapid reconfiguration and safety upgrades, yet introduces upfront procurement complexity and coordination needs that may extend initial facility setup and disrupt ongoing data collection.

name: Hybrid event-triage workflow with clinician-augmented scoring
consequences: By combining algorithmic triage with clinician review at key milestones, this lever improves accuracy of event classification while maintaining review throughput. However, it increases scheduling needs for clinicians and may slow immediate output during peak periods.
options: Implement clinician-augmented triage that flags high-fidelity events for rapid review while auto-classifying routine patterns efficiently.
Adopt adaptive scoring thresholds based on patient cohort to balance sensitivity and false positives during night transitions.
Adopt a lightweight, checklist-driven annotation protocol to standardize manual review while minimizing cognitive load on staff.
review: Hybrid event-triage with clinician input improves accuracy but increases scheduling demands for clinicians, potentially slowing throughput during peak stay weeks.

name: Participant incentive and retention design across stay durations
consequences: Enhanced compensation and amenities improves adherence, reduces dropout risk, and increases data yield. Downstream, budget pressure rises and may constrain other program areas if funding does not keep pace.
options: Structure milestone-based participant engagement with escalating compensation aligned to completion of enhanced-night PSG nights milestones.
Offer flexible scheduling and respite accommodations to minimize fatigue and promote long-stay participation across extended stays.
Implement partner-assisted collateral history collection with caregiver support to boost enrollment quality and retention rates.
review: Enhanced incentives improve retention and data yield, but require careful budgeting and monitoring to avoid creating inequities or unsustainable burn rates.

name: Staffing model resilience and cross-training for night shifts
consequences: Cross-training staff reduces risk of coverage gaps and ensures safety during nights, boosting throughput. Downstream, it increases training overhead and role clarity challenges during initial ramp-up.
options: Establish cross-trained technician teams capable of monitoring multiple suites and performing preliminary scoring on-site during night shifts.
Institute a reserve on-call roster to cover unexpected absences without compromising safety or response time.
Rotate staff across night shifts and day shifts to balance fatigue, coverage, and experience levels.
review: Resilient staffing reduces single-point failures and ensures safety coverage, yet cross-training raises upfront training time and role clarity challenges during initial ramp-up.

name: External collaboration and phased publication milestones
consequences: Engaging external collaborators and publishing incrementally can validate methods and unlock future funding, while potentially slowing internal decision cycles due to review processes.
options: Launch a formal collaboration incubator with selective academia and pharma partners to align on validation milestones.
Publish early-methods papers and data descriptors to demonstrate transparency and attract grant support from diverse funders.
Schedule quarterly progress reviews with the external advisory board to synchronize research aims with funding opportunities.
review: External collaboration and phased publications build credibility and funding prospects, but competing priorities and review cycles may slow internal decision-making and milestone execution.

name: Tiered sensing architecture optimization and data quality gating
consequences: Consequence: This lever reduces participant burden and safety risk by prioritizing noninvasive modalities. Downstream, data processing complexity increases and manual adjudication may become more necessary to maintain accuracy.
options: Consolidate nightly data collection with dry-electrode EEG and mattress sensors for all participants, reserving full PSG for escalation nights.
Preserve full PSG escalation nights for a fixed subset of participants while maintaining base monitoring to retain data richness.
Rotate sensing modalities across cohorts to test modality-specific yields and reduce adaptation effects on sleep architecture.
review: Shifting to noninvasive sensing reduces participant burden and safety risk, but increases data handling complexity and may require more manual adjudication to maintain accuracy.

name: Data governance and privacy preservation plan enforcement
consequences: Consequence: This reduces privacy breach risk and supports regulatory compliance. Downstream, collaboration speed may be limited and external data sharing could require additional approvals.
options: Develop a formal de-identification workflow for all sensor streams and restrict access to bedroom video to authorized personnel only.
Implement tiered access controls with audit logging and periodic privacy impact reviews to ensure compliance with university and legal requirements.
Prohibit internet-enabled data transfers and confine storage to on-site NAS with encrypted backups while enabling de-identified data deposition to secure repositories.
review: Data governance reduces privacy risk but may slow cross-institution collaboration due to approvals and access controls.

name: Recruitment pre-screen and consent pipeline optimization
consequences: Consequence: Expands recruitment stability and reduces late-screening gaps. Downstream, screening complexity and administrative load rise.
options: Centralize structured pre-admission pathway with standardized collateral history collection to improve enrollment efficiency and ensure eligibility consistency across sites.
Diversify regional referrals with remote pre-screening to widen the participant pool while maintaining safety standards.
Introduce non-financial engagement strategies to sustain interest across lengthy stays and reduce dropout risk.
review: Expanding recruitment pathways stabilizes enrollment but increases screening volume, administrative coordination, and scheduling complexity requiring careful process management.

name: Shift design and cross-training for safe 24/7 coverage
consequences: Consequence: Improves safety and throughput through redundancy, but increases scheduling complexity and ongoing competency maintenance requirements that can slow staffing decisions.
options: Institute cross-training across sleep-technician roles to cover nights with minimal fatigue and maintain annotation throughput.
Adopt a pairwise night-shift model with overlapping handoffs to improve event detection and reduce fatigue-related errors.
Pilot a flexible staffing pool with on-call technicians during peak weeks to balance cost and coverage.
review: Cross-training improves safety and throughput through redundancy, but increases scheduling complexity and ongoing competency maintenance requirements that can slow staffing decisions.

name: Expansion gating criteria tied to data quality and staffing resilience
consequences: Consequence: Provides controlled growth anchored to data quality and safety, but audits and metric lag can delay scaling and frustrate funding timelines.
options: Only expand to additional suites once pilot metrics meet predefined data quality and safety thresholds.
Proceed with staged expansion regardless of metrics to accelerate capacity, accepting potential quality trade-offs and rework.
Adopt a flexible expansion plan that scales up to 12 suites contingent on independent data audits and safety reviews.
review: Expansion gating provides controlled growth anchored to data quality and safety, but audits and metric lag can delay scaling and frustrate funding timelines.

name: Event-triage algorithm validation framework
consequences: Consequence: Improves reliability and reduces reviewer fatigue through structured steps. Downstream, setup and training requirements increase and integration with existing lab processes becomes critical.
options: Benchmark scoring against dual human adjudicators and refine rubric to improve agreement without reliance on automation.
Establish a blinded, tiered triage approach that flags probable events for human review in near-real-time while maintaining record integrity.
Introduce a modular annotation workflow splitting tasks between initial detection, corroboration, and final adjudication to optimize throughput.
review: Validation framework clarifies operational expectations and improves data integrity, but may slow early adjudication when real-time throughput demands conflict with rigorous scoring standards.

name: Regulatory and safety-compliance readiness
consequences: Consequence: Strengthens risk management and compliance posture, but adds recurring external costs. Downstream, expansion milestones hinge on external review timing and may impact funding timelines.
options: Implement comprehensive emergency response drills and medical oversight to ensure rapid handling of nocturnal events.
Formalize ethics and safety oversight with monthly reviews and documented incident logging to satisfy regulatory expectations.
Engage external safety consultants to audit facility modifications and staff procedures on a quarterly cadence.
review: Regulatory readiness strengthens compliance and safety oversight, but external reviews introduce scheduling demands that may constrain agile adjustments during early pilot optimization.
